age_suitability.notes: Medicine content. OBSERVED: the child hides prescribed medicine (pours it on food, buries it, puts it in a nest) and offers it to another child in exchange for a toy; a dog carries the bottle in its mouth. These are imitable and two are medication-safety risks (another child drinking it, a pet reaching it); the book frames them as failed jokes, never says they are unsafe. On the positive side the picture shows an adult giving the dose on a spoon. Any MagicPaper use should keep medicine in adult hands, drop the swap with another child and keep animals away from it. Peak research intensity 4 of 5 (the ruined sandwich and the imagined sea), about 2 on the engine's 0-3 scale; illness itself stays at 2 of 5, about 1 on the 0-3 scale; no fear of illness or of the doctor. 139 words, mean sentence 5.4, longest 15: fits 3-4 as read-aloud, also 5-6. Text-only MagicPaper would lose the failures, which live in the pictures.
